title: Agency self-restraint and a defective delegation
shortTitle: Agency self-restraint and a defective delegation
summary: An agency’s voluntary decision to narrow its power cannot supply a legislative standard that Congress constitutionally had to provide.
notes:
Whitman distinguishes interpretation of the power Congress actually granted from an agency’s discretionary choice to exercise only part of that power. Courts determine whether the statute supplies sufficient guidance. If Congress left a constitutionally impermissible legislative choice open, the agency cannot cure the problem by choosing its own limiting rule.

Amalgamated Meat Cutters describes subsidiary administrative standards as supporting accountability and consistency under a validly construed statute. That practical role does not establish that administrative rulemaking can repair an unconstitutional transfer of legislative power. The comparison therefore requires attention to whether the statutory guidance already exists.
